counterCodes.strength: tplsig (A 117 B sha 6098599c, B 171 B sha 5aac73bf): B056 nbkill body (New_Best-derived) with the INT87 search changed to B1 09 31 F6 -> CC CC CC CC (worker-template bytes 9-12, 'mov cl,9; xor si,si'); own worker xor si,si re-encoded 33 F6. Base team score 0.003 (1 copy, 5n2sl), 0.025 (1 copy, aiipe), 0.000 (2 copies, 9tabr), 0.000 (3 copies, ee7fn). Kills SDd and C2 identically.
control (sha 80ea3d6b / 952e4267): same bytes except search B1 09 31 F7 (no match). Base 0.338 (1 copy), 0.192 (2), 0.111 (3).
tplcom dilution variant (sha 80002980 / 69b5eb2f): searches 29 D4 29 2F, a template window shared by ~14 archived field binaries; own sub sp,dx re-encoded 2B E2. Base 0.058 (1 copy, aiipe).

threatFindings.threat: Worker-template signature attack: one early INT87 (counter instr 10/11, std from DI=0) replaces a 4-byte window of the 18-byte worker template in our arena body before phoenix_init copies it to private memory (A turn ~26-34); every later rebuild (and every captured zombie that runs B's phoenix_init) executes CC and dies.
threatFindings.evidence: Threat 5n2sl (1 copy, 160 battles/threat): base team 0.0031 vs tplsig against 0.3375 vs the control tplctl; counter team 0.693 vs 0.512. 9tabr (2 copies, 240 battles): 0.000 vs 0.192. ee7fn (3 copies, no filler): 0.000 vs 0.111. aiipe (1 copy, other cohorts): 0.025. Counter/control cohorts have different random filler teams (unpaired), but the gap is 20-100x the noise.
threatFindings.impact: about -0.33 points/battle per cohort with one copy; total wipe-out at 2-3 copies. Same size as B056's executed-initializer counter (nbkill 0.000 on the same job 5n2sl).

threatFindings.threat: Frontier candidates and the B056 reorder fix are equally exposed (template bytes unchanged)
threatFindings.evidence: SDd (A 103ae804 / B 36e78a91) minus base on tplsig: exactly 0 in 5n2sl, 9tabr, ee7fn; also 0 vs nbkill. C2 (A 36bf5eee) minus base: exactly 0 on tplsig and tplcom (aiipe). B056 fixA/fixB, V6Guard, V6, V4, zchain4 contain B1 09 31 F6 (static scan); reorder fix not run here.
threatFindings.impact: No current or proposed edit closes this hole; it is independent of phoenix_init instruction order.

threatFindings.threat: The worker template is a lineage-wide signature: rev0 worker bytes are byte-identical to New_Best/zchain4 (A5 F3 A5 29 D4 29 2F 8B 3F B1 09 31 F6 AB 4F FF 1F); a counter author must re-encode their own worker (31 F6 -> 33 F6, 29 D4 -> 2B E2) to avoid self-hit, which costs nothing.
threatFindings.evidence: Static scan (2025 senior/young, zombies, cgx2024 live/final2): B1 09 31 F6 only in HRZ_Registered_Winners1/2 besides the V6/New_Best/zchain4 family; 29 D4 29 2F in 14 binaries (cgx123123, stuxnet, Code_Killer, BinaryBandits, VanLavan, GoonSquad, anonymous, Grindo, Registered_Winners, TOM_R_JS). Re-encoded counters work (tplsig/tplcom kill base).
threatFindings.impact: Attack is cheap to build from any published V6/New_Best code.

threatFindings.threat: Field teams carrying the same template window act as natural decoys and dilute a common-window counter
threatFindings.evidence: aiipe (1 copy, 12 cohorts each, unpaired fillers): base 0.058 vs tplcom (common window 29 D4 29 2F) vs 0.025 vs tplsig (rare window). Difference is small and confounded with filler choice; the rare-window counter is the stronger test case.
threatFindings.impact: at most a few hundredths; not a defense

threatFindings.threat: Re-encoding our template (e.g. xor si,si as 33 F6) as a fix
threatFindings.evidence: Not tested. By analogy with B056 x4a43 (a retarget defeats a reorder) a re-encoding only moves the target; 13 other template windows remain.

recommendation: No promotion candidate (counter-code role). Add tplsig (agent2/night/scratch/B076/counterA.asm, counterB.asm) with control ctlA/ctlB to the threat library as the template-data counterpart of B056's executed-initializer counter: it kills rev0, SDd and C2 alike (0.000-0.025/battle vs 0.11-0.34 control) and survives any phoenix_init reorder. A fix role testing it should note that the only by-construction cure is to never keep the template contiguous in the arena (build the 9 private words with mov ax,imm / stosw or similar). That does not close B056's executed-byte hole, and it removes B's natural FF 1F CC CC tail decoy (B066 padB, A022 SDc showed that costs). Recommend treating domain 6 as an accepted, low-field-exposure risk (no archived team searches these windows) rather than spending bytes on it.
